At actual size this reads as a wobble or misregistration, not as land. On the back every spirits row rule is dead straight, so the 'level line of h' conceit is invisible on page 2.

concept_verdict: HILERAS is a real, ownable thesis: Iowa corn rows and Jalisco agave rows as one planted field. That places it well above festive trim. It still does not govern the page. The field is a header band, and below it sits a conventional three-up list whose only trace of the land is a hairline that bends a few pixels. Half of the thesis is missing: there is no corn anywhere. The hero's saturated pinstriped brown, tan, black and teal bands still read as a sarape or a 1970s retro wave, not as an aerial survey. That is the costume read the brief tried to kill, now with contour lines. At actual size the teal 'plan-view rosettes' read as starbursts or snowflakes, not agave. Against ref-solstice and ref-01 (the Bistro): those boards use one image family with real materiality (paper, gold leaf, stone, torn edges), and the art physically frames and leads into the type column. Here the art stops at a hard horizontal edge and the type never meets it. Substitution test: swap the hero for any generic topographic-wave stock graphic and the menu below would not change. That is a fail. The strongest idea on the page is the back-page survey table: the oak-months axis, the NOM column and survey-red prices. It is the one place where the 'survey of the field' thesis produces information design, not decoration.
remove: The teal agave starbursts, first the whole back-page head band of them, which is pure trim, and then the dotted strings of them in the front hero. They are the costume device, and the contour field reads more like a survey without them.
top_problem: The concept is a header, not a system. The boldest missing idea is to make the page itself the aerial field: corn hileras and agave hileras as the actual row structure every item sits in, across both pages, with the land meeting and framing the type rather than stopping at a hard edge above it.
fixes: Lock one true 3-column grid on the front: every name in a column at one x (Paloma, House Daiquiri and Milpa to one edge; Ranch Water, Mezcal Negroni and Loess to one edge), with the proposed ring hanging in the gutter outside that edge.

Carry the field onto both pages as structure, not trim: let the terrain run down one edge or under the section strips so the land meets the type, and render the back-page row rules as the same level lines (gently bent) instead of straight table rules.

Put the Iowa half of the thesis on the page: draw corn rows (plan-view stalks or tassel stipple, same line weight and shadow rule as the agave) in alternating hileras with agave, so the substitution test passes and the image cannot be swapped for generic topo art.

Break the sarape read in the hero: drop the black and saturated tan pinstripe bands to 2 earth values plus 1 teal crop value, replace the pinstripes with sparse furrow hatching, and add one survey-paper materiality cue (grain or registration offset) with its contrast dropped near text.

Kill the dead zones: fix the 114 px draft-column gap by not syncing to the SIDRA head, pull the wine key up or fill the wine column, and collapse the four 'recipe to confirm' lines in zero proof into one flagged note so the front's bottom band has a job.

lens: every item and price against expanded-v2/manifest.json: single prices, pour columns, bottle prices, flights, price evidence
top_problem: Every printed price matches the manifest, but the content has weak spots. There are no beer ABVs on any row. The tasting lines are class-level and repeat word for word (8 blancos, 7 reposados, 5 añejos and 6 mezcals share lines). Some manifest prices are commercially implausible and are printed without comment: Don Julio 1942 is $25 (n=1) against Cincoro $28 and Clase Azul Reposado $26, and flights are priced at the full sum of pours ($45 Reserve against a corpus flight median of $22). So the menu is price-accurate but not yet a beverage director's list.
problems: I checked all 65 items one by one against the manifest and found no price errors. That covers 32 single prices, 33 × 3 pour prices, 3 wine copa/botella pairs and 3 flights. The pour rule (2/3 and 4/3 of the 1½ oz price, rounded) checks out on every row, for example Fortaleza 13/20/27, Clase Azul 17/26/35 and Cincoro 19/28/37. Each flight equals the sum of its three 1 oz pours: 7+7+13=27, 7+9+10=26, 13+17+15=45.

Tres Generaciones Añejo: the manifest region 'Tequila Valley' is dropped from print. There is a note in gates.json, but the reason given (it shares NOM 1102 with Hornitos, whose region is null) is backwards. The manifest has a region for this row, so it is dropping a sourced fact, not avoiding an unsourced one.

Two brewery lines are rewritten away from the manifest text, as a coordinator deviation. Tecate now reads 'Tecate, B.C.' instead of 'Tecate, Baja California'. Amber Lager drops ', Mexico' and 'Cervecería'.

Two prices differ from Rob's reference image: Ranch Water is 12 where the reference showed 11.50, and Del Maguey Vida is 14 where it showed 11. Both follow the manifest and both rows are ringed, but the ring means 'proposed', not 'price changed from your reference'. Rob needs to sign off on these explicitly.
Beer: no row shows its ABV. The only flag is 'beer ABV to confirm' in the wine-column key, far from the 10 beer rows it applies to. Criterion 8 requires style + ABV on every beer.

Spirit descriptions are only class boilerplate: every blanco reads 'Unaged · peppery, bright cooked agave'. The type/age requirement is met, but nothing tells one bottle from another. Maestro Dobel Diamante is a cristalino and is described as a plain añejo.

The ring on the pour header (proposed size rule) covers all three columns. On the approved Casa rows, though, the 1½ oz prices (12/16/18) are approved and only the 1 oz and 2 oz prices are proposed. The status of each column is ambiguous.

The pour column heads are crowded: '1 oz' and '1½ oz' nearly touch. The wine head reads 'copa ·' with a stray separator. The copa price sits about 45% of the column width away from short names like 'Malbec'. A furrow rule guides the eye across, so this is not a gate fail, but the travel is long.

Section order and flow: Casa · House pours (the manifest's first spirits group, holding the approved items) is buried at the bottom of the right column, below mezcal. Beer and wine come last on the back page, after 33 spirit rows. For a cantina, beer is a primary category, and here it reads as an afterthought.
The manifest flags a dairy allergen (unconfirmed) on Brown Butter Old Fashioned. Nothing on the menu flags it and no allergen note is carried.
fixes: Add each beer's ABV to its brewery line as soon as it is sourced. Until then, print 'ABV tbc' on each beer row instead of one key line in the wine column.
Restore 'Tequila Valley' on Tres Generaciones Añejo exactly as the manifest has it. Print the Tecate and Dos Equis brewery lines verbatim, or record the shortened text back into the manifest.

Split the proposed-size ring onto the 1 oz and 2 oz column heads only, so the approved 1½ oz prices are not marked as proposed. Add a note that flight prices are the sum of the pours and are pending Rob's pricing decision. Flag Don Julio 1942 $25 (n=1) and the Rob-reference price changes (Ranch Water, Vida) to Rob before print.

lens: ingredient names, tasting lines, brewery/producer lines, description completeness
top_problem: The printed stack follows the rule, but the spirits descriptions stop at the category. 33 spirit rows share only 4 tasting lines, one each for blanco, reposado, añejo and espadín. So Casamigos, Patrón and El Jimador read the same, and Clase Azul reads the same as Hornitos. On top of that, several cocktail, beer and wine descriptions are missing a required part and are not flagged.
problems: Spirits (criterion 8): every blanco prints 'Unaged · peppery, bright cooked agave' (8 rows plus the house pour), every reposado '2–12 months oak · vanilla, softened agave' (9), every añejo '1–3 years oak · caramel, dried fruit, baking spice' (5 plus the house pour), and 6 of 7 mezcals 'Pit-roasted espadín · smoke, green fruit'. These are class labels repeated as tasting lines, so the guest cannot tell brands apart. Only the NOM and the price differ.

Maestro Dobel Diamante is a cristalino (a charcoal-filtered, multi-aged blend). It is printed under Añejo with a full oak bar and 'caramel, dried fruit, baking spice'. The class and tasting line need checking against the source. For now it is a verify flag, not a gate fail, because the manifest is the source.

Beer (criterion 8 requires style + ABV): no row shows an ABV. The only flag is 'beer ABV to confirm', which sits in the wine column's key, away from the 10 beer rows. 'Hop-forward draft IPA' largely repeats the item name.

Wine (grape + region): Brut Rosé → 'Ruffino Sparkling Rosé · Italy' gives no grape and no DOC or region. The item name (Brut Rosé) and producer line (Sparkling Rosé) also disagree. The tasting lines 'Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine' and 'Dry sparkling rosé' are category labels, not tasting notes.

Cocktail gaps with no missing_ingredients flag: the Manhattan prints only 'rye whiskey · sweet vermouth', with no bitters. Carajillo shows no garnish, only 'rocks'. Spicy Pineapple Margarita gives no citrus or sweetener and no garnish; it is flagged 'recipe to confirm', which is correct. Check each against the recipe_versions row: either print the missing part or flag it.

Zero proof: 'recipe to confirm' fills the ingredient slot on all four, and none has a garnish or glass line. On Jarritos, 'recipe to confirm' makes no sense for a bottled soda; it should read 'flavour to confirm' or list the flavours.

Unknown NOM and region are left blank with no flag. Casa Noble, Gran Coramino and all mezcals have an empty NOM, yet the column header still reads NOM. El Jimador, Espolòn, Milagro, Casamigos, Teremana, Clase Azul, Dobel and Cincoro show no region. The scorecard says unknowns must be flagged, not silently dropped.
Category treatment: Cognac VSOP is filed under 'Casa · House pours' next to the house tequilas. The house well pours, the cheapest way in, are buried at the bottom of column 2 below the mezcals.

The brewery line format is inconsistent. Most read 'Brewery · City'. Amber Lager reads 'Dos Equis Ámbar · Cuauhtémoc Moctezuma', a brand plus a brewery with no place, so the slot changes meaning partway down the column.

Section order differs between print and phone. Print runs spirits → flights → beer/wine; phone puts beer/wine before spirits. Zero proof sits on the front and beer on the back, so the drinks categories do not get equal treatment across the two pages.

Price format (criterion 3): prices are whole dollars, in red, and consistent everywhere. The spirits pour columns have 0.0 px spread and each row has its own rule, and the flight sums check (7+7+13=27, 7+9+10=26, 13+17+15=45). But the table header '1 oz 1½ oz' crowds together, and the wine header reads 'copa ·' with a stray dot.
fixes: Replace the class-level spirits lines with one distinguishing fact per brand drawn from verified data (for example still or column, tahona or roller mill, cask type, agave estate). Where no fact is on file, print the class line once in the sub-head (for example 'TEQUILA · BLANCO — unaged, peppery, bright cooked agave'), not on every row.

Add ABV to every beer row, or print a visible per-row 'ABV tbc' flag. Move the 'beer ABV to confirm' key into the beer band. Rewrite 'Hop-forward draft IPA' so it gives hop character rather than repeating the name.
Give Brut Rosé its grape(s) and a region or DOC, match the item name to the producer line, and swap the three 'Dry red/white/sparkling' category labels for real tasting notes or a flag.

Check the Manhattan (bitters), Carajillo (garnish) and Dobel Diamante (cristalino class and oak bar) against recipe_versions and the brand facts. Print what is verified and flag the rest with missing_ingredients. Change Jarritos to 'flavour to confirm'.

Show unknown NOM and region as a visible 'tbc' mark instead of a blank. Move Cognac VSOP out of Casa into its own 'Otros · Other' line. Make the Amber Lager brewery line follow 'Brewery · City' like the others. Use the same section order on print and phone.

lens: flow and reading path, front and back, Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar, Iowa City
top_problem: The printed order is Classics, House, Zero proof, then Spirits (33 rows), Flights, and finally Beer/cider/wine squeezed into the bottom third of the back. In a Mexican cantina, beer and the house pours are the first thing most guests look for, and here they are the last thing on the back. The phone puts beer and wine ahead of spirits, so print and phone do not follow the same path.
problems: Section order on the back runs Spirits, Flights, Beer/cider/wine. The core cantina categories (Modelo, Pacifico, Tecate, Draft) are buried at the bottom after a dense 33-row table. The phone uses a different order (beer/wine before spirits), which breaks coherence between print and phone.

Casa · House pours (the well-priced entry point) sits last, at the foot of the right spirits column. It also mixes Cognac VSOP with the tequilas under the same head, so a guest reading from the top never reaches the house pours first.

Each class tasting line is repeated on every row: 'Unaged · peppery, bright cooked agave' appears 9 times (8 blancos plus the house blanco), 'Pit-roasted espadín · smoke, green fruit' 7 times, and '2–12 months oak · vanilla, softened agave' 9 times. That doubles the table's line count without telling one bottle from another. These lines are class facts, not item descriptions, so criterion 8 is only partly met for the 33 spirits.
The back page has two competing entry points: the 'Destilados · Spirits' head and the oak scale and key block top right, which is as heavy as the head.

The front furrow rules start at one item's price and run into the next item's proposed ring (Margarita 15 to Paloma, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16 to House Daiquiri, Nojito 8 to Agua de Jamaica). They read as leaders that end at the neighbouring item. Association still passes because each price sits within 0.68 em of its own name, but the rule points the eye the wrong way.

Zero proof has no ingredients (flagged 'recipe to confirm', which is correct). The flag lines float about 1 line below the sensory lines and are followed by a key, then roughly 8% dead canvas at the foot of the front. The back also ends with an unused band under Draft and Cans.
Beer rows have no ABV. It is flagged only once, in a global key ('beer ABV to confirm') rather than per row, so criterion 8 (style + ABV) is unmet for all 10 beers and the cider.

Price format has minor faults: the pour header is cramped ('1 oz1½ oz' nearly touches), the wine header reads 'copa ·' with a stray dot, and the gap above Modelo Especial is larger than the other draft gaps.

Brewery lines are abridged from the manifest: Tecate drops 'Cervecería' and 'Baja California' becomes 'B.C.'; Amber Lager drops 'Cervecería' and ', Mexico'. Both are declared coordinator deviations and not invented, but they are still changed printed text.
fixes: Reorder the back to Cerveza (Draft, then Cans + Cider), then Vino, then Destilados with Casa · House pours first, then Flights (or Flights directly after the tequila classes), and make the phone use exactly the same order.

Move each class tasting line up to its class subhead (for example 'TEQUILA · BLANCO — unaged · peppery, bright cooked agave') and keep only the region and any item-specific note on each row, which cuts the spirits table by about 30 lines.
End each front furrow rule at the price, or send it back toward the column's own left edge, so no rule runs from one item's price into the next item's ring.
Put a per-row 'ABV to confirm' in each beer's brewery line (or style + ABV once known), and set the zero-proof 'recipe to confirm' directly under the sensory line to close the gap.

Shrink the oak scale and key into a single quiet line under the Destilados head, fix the '1 oz 1½ oz' header spacing and the 'copa ·' dot, and use the freed front-foot and back-foot space for the reordered beer block instead of empty canvas.

lens: voice and consistency of descriptions; bilingual headings and venue copy; venue-type fit (Mexican restaurant + cocktail bar, Iowa City)
top_problem: The descriptions have two different voices. The cocktail sensory lines are item-specific and appetising ('Toasted corn, cacao, oak'; 'Soft smoke, honey, ginger snap'). But the spirits, wine and beer lines are class boilerplate: 'Unaged · peppery, bright cooked agave' appears word for word on all 8 blancos plus the house blanco, '2–12 months oak · vanilla, softened agave' on all 9 reposados, 'Pit-roasted espadín · smoke, green fruit' on 7 of 8 mezcals, and the wine lines are 'Dry red wine / Dry white wine / Dry sparkling rosé'. On the back page, which carries 33 of the 65 items, the reader cannot tell Patrón from Siete Leguas, or Clase Azul from Hornitos, from the copy. That is taxonomy wording, not guest language.
problems: Content integrity holds. I spot-checked the printed prices, sensory lines, ingredients, garnish/glass, brewery and producer lines against expanded-v2/manifest.json and they match (Margarita 15, Paloma 12, Ranch Water 12, Nojito 8, Agua de Jamaica 5, Horchata 4, Jarritos 4, Malbec 12/42, Pinot Grigio 11/40, Brut Rosé 13/45, beer brewery lines). The 3-size pour rule (PROPOSED) carries its ring in the table header. The declared deviations (Tres Generaciones region omitted; Tecate and Dos Equis brewery lines shortened) are logged in gates.json. No tagline or prop caption states an item fact.

Unflagged drafts: many sensory lines are sensory_status 'draft_not_tasted' in the manifest (for example Manhattan, Paloma, Ranch Water), yet they print with the same authority as the DB-sourced Margarita line. Approved_db rows like Manhattan carry no ring, so a drafted tasting claim reads as confirmed fact.

Spirits tasting lines are one line per class, repeated verbatim. They describe the category, not the bottle, so the 1½ oz price column is the only thing that tells 33 rows apart. Mezcal 'Pit-roasted espadín' on every row including Del Maguey Chichicapa and Sombra reads as copy-paste. Ilegal Joven is the only row with its own line.

Beer and wine descriptions are taxonomy wording or restate the name: 'Hop-forward draft IPA' under 'Dry-Hopped IPA'; 'Crisp pale lager' under 'Czech Pilsner'; 'Dry red wine' under 'Malbec'. The wine rows name no grape for the Brut Rosé (Ruffino Sparkling Rosé names none). No beer shows an ABV; it is flagged only once in a footnote key ('beer ABV to confirm'), not per row.

Zero proof: all four drinks show 'recipe to confirm'. That flag is correct, but it leaves the NA section as name + price + three words. Nojito's 'Mint, lime, soda' reads as an ingredient list in the sensory slot while the ingredient slot says 'recipe to confirm', which is contradictory.

Bilingual system is inconsistent across levels. Level-1 heads are Spanish italic · English roman (good). Level-2 heads mix three patterns: 'DE BARRIL · DRAFT' and 'EN LATA · CANS' (ES · EN); 'TEQUILA · BLANCO', 'TEQUILA · AÑEJO' and 'MEZCAL' (Spanish category · class, no English); 'CASA · HOUSE POURS' (ES · EN with a different noun count). The manifest wine head 'Por copa y botella · Glass & bottle' was replaced by 'VINO · WINE', and the column labels are Spanish-only 'copa ·' / 'botella', with a stray trailing middle dot after 'copa'.

Flight names double the bilingual convention ('Vuelo de Tequila · Tequila Flight'). This makes the longest name-to-price gap on the letter page (the measured inline worst case). Every other item name is monolingual.

Cognac VSOP sits under 'CASA · HOUSE POURS' between house tequilas, and no cocktail uses it (Carajillo is Licor 43 + espresso). A cognac inside an agave survey is a venue-fit oddity with no heading or explanation.

Section order and venue fit: in print, beer (the high-volume category at a Mexican cantina in a college town) is the last band on the back page, under 33 spirits rows. The phone puts beer and wine ahead of spirits, so print and phone read in different orders. The front bottom has about 5% unused cream below the NA key.

Venue copy: the wordmark 'Cantina' plus '& Cocktail Bar · Iowa City, Iowa' is honest and generic. Nothing in the printed copy names the Iowa and Jalisco row-crop thesis, so the land-to-agave idea reads only through art, never through words, except Loess, Milpa Old Fashioned and the Iowa wildflower honey syrup. That is appropriate restraint, not a defect.
fixes: Replace the class-boilerplate spirits lines with bottle-specific tasting lines from verified producer notes. Until those exist, print only the class line once per sub-head (for example under 'TEQUILA · BLANCO') and leave the row line as region/NOM, rather than repeating the same sentence 9 times.

Mark every sensory line whose manifest sensory_status is 'draft_not_tasted' with the proposed ring, or a distinct 'tasting note to confirm' treatment, so drafted claims on approved rows are not presented as fact.

Rewrite the beer and wine sensory lines so they add information beyond the name (hop character, malt, fruit), and add a per-row 'ABV —' slot for beer. Name the grape(s) for the Brut Rosé, or flag 'grape to confirm' on that row.

Unify level-2 headings to one ES · EN pattern: 'TEQUILA BLANCO · UNAGED', 'MEZCAL · MEZCAL' or equivalent, 'VINO · WINE' with 'copa · glass / botella · bottle' column labels. Drop the stray trailing dot after 'copa'.

Move Cognac VSOP out of the house-tequila group into its own one-line 'Otros · Other' sub-head. Make the print section order match the phone (beer and wine before the spirits survey), or state why print leads with spirits.

lens: missing data: how proposed rows, brewery/producer proposals, the pour-size rule, 'recipe to confirm' and ABV are flagged; anything invented
top_problem: The flags are uneven. The two most speculative recipes (Milpa Old Fashioned and Loess, which the manifest says are 'recipe to be written and costed') print full ingredient lists as if final, with only the ring. Spicy Pineapple Margarita does get 'recipe to confirm'. Beer ABV, which the scorecard requires, is missing from all 10 beer rows and is covered only by a loose staff note, 'beer ABV to confirm', in the wine column that no row points to.
problems: Nothing is invented. I compared the DOM text of menu.html with expanded-v2/manifest.json: all 32 single prices, 99 pour prices, 3 bottle prices and 3 flight prices match. The flight sums check out (7+7+13=27, 7+9+10=26, 13+17+15=45). Every sensory line, ingredient, garnish, glass, NOM and region traces to the manifest, and null NOM/region cells are left blank rather than filled.

Proposed rows are flagged correctly: 60 row rings, which covers every PROPOSED and rob_reference_image row (8 cocktails, 30 spirits, 6 beers, 4 zero proof, 3 flights) plus 2 pour-size header rings. Approved rows (Margarita, Manhattan, Brown Butter Old Fashioned, House Daiquiri, the 3 house pours) have no ring. But the ring is on about 57 of 65 rows, so it stops telling the reader anything. One glyph also stands for four different things: new item, reference-image item, proposed brewery/producer, and proposed pour rule.

Brewery and producer proposals on approved rows (Czech Pilsner, Dry-Hopped IPA, Amber Lager, Dry Cider, Malbec, Pinot Grigio, Brut Rosé) correctly carry the ring on the brewery/producer line, not the name line. Good. Amber Lager is the weak one: its line 'Dos Equis Ámbar · Cuauhtémoc Moctezuma' names a different branded product, so it reads as a fact about what is poured.

The pour-size rule (status PROPOSED; 1 oz = 2/3 and 2 oz = 4/3 of the corpus 1.5 oz median) is flagged only by a very small ring after '2 oz' in each table header. On the approved house pours (Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila, Cognac VSOP), the 1 oz and 2 oz prices come from this proposed rule but sit in rows with no ring, so a reader cannot tell which of those prices are approved.

'recipe to confirm' is styled correctly as span.flag on the 4 zero-proof items and on Spicy Pineapple Margarita. But Milpa Old Fashioned (house roasted-corn syrup, mole bitters) and Loess (Iowa wildflower honey syrup, ginger) are unwritten, uncosted recipes in the manifest and carry no 'recipe to confirm'. Their ingredient lists read as final.

ABV: no beer row has an ABV (the manifest has none), and criterion 8 requires style + ABV. The only flag is the plain-text line 'beer ABV to confirm' under the ring key in the wine column. It has no glyph and no link to any row, and it reads as a production note printed on the guest menu.
Wine: Brut Rosé has no grape and a region of only 'Italy', and neither gap is flagged. Malbec and Pinot Grigio name their grapes; Brut Rosé does not.

The NOM-sharing rule is applied inconsistently. Tres Generaciones Añejo's manifest region ('Tequila Valley') was dropped because NOM 1102 is shared with Hornitos (region null). Yet Herradura Reposado prints 'Tequila Valley' even though it shares NOM 1119 with El Jimador (region null). This is a documented coordinator deviation, not an invention, but the logic is not consistent.

Tasting lines are identical class-level text on 8 blancos, 9 reposados, 5 añejos and 7 of 8 mezcals, and every one is 'draft_not_tasted' in the manifest. The identical lines do not tell the pours apart, and nothing shows they are untasted drafts. Maestro Dobel Diamante is a cristalino but prints the plain añejo line ('caramel') with no cristalino note.

Order: in print the sequence is cocktails, zero proof, spirits, flights, then beer/cider/wine. On the phone, beer and wine come before spirits, so the two formats disagree. In print, beer and wine (a core category for an Iowa City cantina) are buried at the bottom of the back page, and the approved house pours sit last, after the mezcals.

Thin-evidence prices (n=1 or 2: Olmeca Altos Plata, Don Julio 1942, El Tesoro, Cincoro, El Jimador, Gran Coramino) are shown as firm prices. The ring covers them as proposals, which passes, but they are not marked as more tentative than well-evidenced prices.
fixes: Add the span.flag 'recipe to confirm' to Milpa Old Fashioned and Loess, matching Spicy Pineapple Margarita, because the manifest says those recipes are not yet written or costed.
Replace the loose 'beer ABV to confirm' note with an ABV slot on each beer row, e.g. 'Crisp pale lager · ABV to confirm' in the flag style, so every beer row shows its missing ABV.

Split the ring key into two glyphs: one for a proposed item or price, one for a proposed brewery/producer/pour rule. Also give the pour-size header ring its own key line, 'pour sizes and 1 oz / 2 oz prices proposed', so the derived prices on the approved house pours are visibly flagged.

Apply the NOM-sharing region rule both ways: either drop 'Tequila Valley' from Herradura Reposado (NOM 1119 is shared with El Jimador) or restore it to Tres Generaciones. Also add a 'grape to confirm' flag to Brut Rosé.

Make print and phone use one section order, and move beer, cider and wine up (for example cocktails, beer/wine, spirits and flights, zero proof), with the house pours leading the spirits table instead of trailing the mezcals.

lens: description quality and one guest-facing voice (K1v2 HILERAS, /home/user/phg-harmony-app/handoff/designs/test-1-iowa-city-cantina/explore-K1v2/)
top_problem: There are two voices on this menu and only the cocktails get the good one. The 12 cocktails have short, appetising sensory lines ('Green heat, ripe pineapple'; 'Soft smoke, honey, ginger snap'). The 33 spirits have 4 class-level notes pasted onto every row. All 8 blancos read 'Unaged · peppery, bright cooked agave'. All 9 reposados read '2–12 months oak · vanilla, softened agave'. The 5 añejos share one añejo note, and 7 of the 8 mezcals read 'Pit-roasted espadín · smoke, green fruit'. The manifest itself marks these sensory_status 'class-level (NOM-006 age classes / mezcal category)'. Beer, wine, cider and soda slip into taxonomy that just repeats the item: 'Dry red wine' (Malbec), 'Dry white wine' (Pinot Grigio), 'Dry sparkling rosé' (Brut Rosé), 'Dry sparkling cider' (Dry Cider), 'Hop-forward draft IPA' (Dry-Hopped IPA), 'Crisp pale lager' (Czech Pilsner), 'Mexican fruit soda' (Jarritos). On top of that, back-office words are printed to the guest: 'recipe to confirm' x5, 'beer ABV to confirm', 'months in oak (class range)', a 'NOM' column and 'proposed — pending approval'.
problems: C12 taxonomy / copy-paste: 30 of 33 spirit notes are 4 repeated class strings, so a guest cannot tell Patrón Silver from Siete Leguas or Hornitos from Fortaleza. Source: expanded-v2/manifest.json spirits[].sensory_status = 'class-level … draft, not tasted'.
C12 name-repeat: the wine, cider, IPA, pilsner and Jarritos lines only restate the category or name. Source: manifest wine[].sensory, beer_cider[].sensory, zero_proof[Jarritos].sensory.

C12 voice break: 'recipe to confirm' is printed in the ingredient slot of Nojito, Agua de Jamaica, Horchata and Jarritos, and inline after 'fresh pineapple' in Spicy Pineapple Margarita. With 'beer ABV to confirm' and 'months in oak (class range)', this is internal workflow language on a guest page. The flagging itself is correct (proposal.md line 45); the wording is not guest copy.

lens: Venue fit for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City, IA (census context, price tier), plus ingredient accuracy, description quality and how descriptions sit with prices
top_problem: The drinks list is deep enough for a real cantina: 25 tequilas with correct NOMs (Siete Leguas 1120, Fortaleza 1493, El Tesoro 1139, Patrón 1492, Corralejo 1368), 8 Oaxacan mezcals, and Iowa-rooted house drinks (Milpa, Loess, Big Grove, Backpocket). The guest-facing copy lets it down. The 33 spirit tasting lines are class-level text repeated word for word: 'Unaged · peppery, bright cooked agave' appears 9 times, '2–12 months oak · vanilla, softened agave' 10 times, '1–3 years oak · caramel, dried fruit, baking spice' 6 times and 'Pit-roasted espadín · smoke, green fruit' 7 times. The wine and beer lines read like database classes ('Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine', 'Crisp pale lager', 'Hop-forward draft IPA'). On top of that, the order undersells what this downtown crowd drinks most. ZCTA 52240 (phg_census_zcta: median age 28.6, 29.9% aged 21–34, median household income $52,960, 26.1% of households over $100k, 11% Hispanic/Latino) and 52246 (36.9% aged 21–34) point to beer and approachable cocktails, yet beer and cider sit in the last band of the back page, below a 99-price, three-size pour grid.
problems: C11 (manifest Manhattan row, source 'rv 9fb77eaa (bitters hidden: public_components)'): the menu prints 'rye whiskey · sweet vermouth' only. The venue recipe does have bitters, so the printed spec is traceable but incomplete, and any bartender reading it will take it as a mistake.

C11 (manifest Maestro Dobel Diamante note 'Diamante is a cristalino añejo; class set to añejo'): the menu gives it the full añejo oak bar and the line 'caramel, dried fruit, baking spice'. A guest who orders it gets a clear spirit, and nothing on the menu says cristalino.

C11/C10 (manifest mezcal rows: Ilegal Joven sensory 'Unaged, pit-roasted'; the other espadíns have oak 'not stated'): only Ilegal Joven carries the unaged dot. That implies the other seven jovenes (Vida, Sombra, Vago and the rest) are aged, which is an implied fact with no source.

C11 (manifest Tres Generaciones Añejo region = 'Tequila Valley'): the coordinator removed the region, so the menu drops a correct, sourced fact while Herradura and Fortaleza keep theirs. It is conservative, but it makes the table inconsistent. Tres Generaciones is Sauza, from Tequila town.
C12: across 33 spirit rows only the region changes the tasting line. The survey table reads as NOM-006 class definitions, not guest language, and the brief asked for 'expand the descriptions'.

C12: the cocktail sensory lines are good (Batanga 'Cola-dark, salty, sharp lime', Loess 'Soft smoke, honey, ginger snap'). But House Daiquiri 'Crisp, clean, lightly rich' contradicts itself, Horchata 'Rice, cinnamon, creamy' is an ingredient list, and Jarritos shows 'recipe to confirm' under a bottled soda, where flavours belong.
C13: Cognac VSOP (approved_db) is filed under 'CASA · HOUSE POURS' in a Mexican spirits survey, and it breaks the tequila/mezcal story. It belongs in a separate 'Otros' line.

C13: 'Tipsy in Tijuana Mexican Lager' (PROPOSED, Backpocket Brewing · Coralville) is a jokey border-town name on a menu that otherwise treats Mexico with respect (the 'style is not costume' rule). Because it is PROPOSED it can be dropped, and a local lager is the better slot.

C13: price tier. Cocktails at $12–16 sit at the top of downtown Iowa City for a market with a $53k median household income. That is defensible for a craft bar, but the top of the menu leans premium: Reserve flight $45, Clase Azul 1½ oz $26, Cincoro $28. Meanwhile the 1 oz / 1½ oz / 2 oz grid (spirit_pour_sizes, PROPOSED) triples the price count for a student-and-grad crowd that orders 'a shot' or 'a pour'.

C13: the only cider is Strongbow Original Dry · Hereford, England (manifest 'style match proposal'). Wilson's Orchard in Iowa City is the obvious local-cider opportunity, but it needs a data row before it can be printed.

C14 front: because items in a row share a baseline (margin-top:auto), Spicy Pineapple Margarita's serve line is just 'rocks', stranded under an empty line. On the zero-proof row, 'recipe to confirm' floats about 1 line below each sensory line, which reads as an orphan.

C14 back: the pour header '1 oz 1½ oz' is set nearly touching with no gap between them. Region is tacked onto the italic tasting run in a second typeface, so Olmeca, Patrón and Don Julio 1942 lines run the full measure and crowd the NOM and oak axis. The wine header 'copa ·' has a stray trailing dot.

C14: the Vuelo Reserva line 'Highland oak, lowland agave, deep mineral smoke' is in the opposite order to its item list (Fortaleza Reposado = Tequila Valley/lowland, then El Tesoro Añejo = Los Altos/highland). 'Mineral' traces only to the manifest's draft line, not to a product row. It is close to an association problem but does not fail the gate.

lens: How descriptions and prices sit together on the print PNGs: inline prices, the 1 oz / 1½ oz / 2 oz pour columns, wine copa/botella, and the price-to-item gate. The manifest cites rv f06abb74 (Margarita) and rv 9fb77eaa (Manhattan).
top_problem: The spirits table is priced well, but its descriptions are taxonomy lines stamped on every row. 'Unaged · peppery, bright cooked agave' appears on 9 rows. '2–12 months oak · vanilla, softened agave' appears on 9 rows. 'Pit-roasted espadín · smoke, green fruit' appears on 7 rows. '1–3 years oak · caramel, dried fruit, baking spice' appears on 6 rows. Wine is 'Dry red wine' / 'Dry white wine'. This is database class wording, not guest language, and it makes 33 pours read as 4. The pour grid also has crowded headers: '1 oz1½ oz' nearly touch in both columns (back ~x980-1150 and ~x2550-2720 at 2550 px), and the proposed ring hangs after '2 oz'. Price association holds. Every inline price is within 0.7 em of its name on the same line. The pour and wine columns have 0.00 px right-edge spread, with a furrow rule on each row. Flight sums check out: 7+7+13=27, 7+9+10=26, 13+17+15=45. Weak spots: the furrow rule leaves a price and runs straight into the next item's ring ('Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16 —— House Daiquiri', 'Mezcal Flight 26 —— ○ Vuelo Reserva'). The wine leader stops about 100 px short of the copa price. The wine header 'copa ·  botella' has a stray middle dot and is the only label with no English. Factual items to verify, not fails: Maestro Dobel Diamante is a cristalino (clear, filtered blend) but is printed under Añejo as '1–3 years oak · caramel, dried fruit'. 'Brut Rosé' is paired with Ruffino Sparkling Rosé; confirm that bottling is labelled Brut and not Extra Dry. 'Cognac VSOP' filed under 'Casa · House pours' in a Destilados table weakens venue fit. Jarritos, a bottled soda, prints 'recipe to confirm'. Zero proof has no serve line, and the 4-up row leaves an empty band between the sensory line and the flag.
fixes: Replace the repeated class-level tasting lines with one class note per sub-head (for example under TEQUILA · REPOSADO: '2–12 months in oak: vanilla, softened agave'). Keep the per-row second line for sourced facts only (NOM, region). If a brand has a sourced note, print that instead. Rewrite 'Dry red wine' / 'Dry white wine' / 'Hop-forward draft IPA' in guest language drawn from producer and style rows.

Space the pour header labels to the width of their right-aligned number columns (at least 1 em between '1 oz' and '1½ oz'), and move the proposed ring in front of the header group, not after '2 oz'. Drop the stray dot in 'copa ·' and add a gloss ('copa · glass / botella · bottle'), since every other label is bilingual.

Stop each furrow rule at least 1 em before the next item's ring or name, so no rule reads as a leader from one item's price into the next item (De la Casa row 1, Spicy Pineapple → Milpa, Flights). Run the wine leader all the way to the copa price.

Verify Maestro Dobel Diamante's class in public.brand_products / spirit_lexicon. Either move it to a cristalino label or drop the oak-range tasting line. Confirm that Ruffino Sparkling Rosé matches 'Brut' before print.

On Jarritos, change 'recipe to confirm' to 'flavours to confirm'. Move Cognac VSOP out of 'Casa · House pours' into its own labelled row. Give the zero-proof items a serve line, or close the empty band so the flag does not float.
